          Bayern Munich vs Arsenal Prediction: UEFA Champions League Preview
        
      
                          
                      Oct 20, 2026
          
                      Harry Carr / Author
                  
      
              
                      
                  
          

    
              
      
              
                    
Two of the pre-season UEFA Champions League favourites go head-to-head in Bavaria on Wednesday, and we look ahead to that clash with our data-powered Bayern Munich vs Arsenal prediction and preview.
Going into Matchday 3 of the league phase in this season's UEFA Champions League, Arsenal and Bayern Munich are the Opta supercomputer's top two favourites to become European champions.
The predictive model gives Arsenal a 20.7% chance of lifting the trophy for the first time, while Bayern have a 15.2% probability of clinching their seventh continental crown.
And with the teams going head-to-head at the Allianz Arena on Wednesday, both will face an early test of their credentials.

Bayern got back to winning ways in convincing fashion in the Bundesliga on Saturday, as a Luis Díaz hat-trick helped them thump RB Leipzig 6-1. The Bavarian giants had a staggering 17 shots on target in that match, their most in any league game since tallying 20 against Borussia Mönchengladbach in August 2022.

That dominant victory must have been cathartic following a frustrating return from the international break for Vincent Kompany's side, who had to come from behind twice to draw 2-2 with Augsburg in their previous Bundesliga game, before sharing six goals equally with Norwegian champions Viking on MD2 in the Champions League.

Michael Olise‘s red card was costly in that game, not only because it allowed Viking to play the final 16 minutes with a numerical advantage, scoring a late equaliser, but also because the France superstar will now serve a one-match ban against Arsenal.

Olise will leave big shoes to fill. Since the start of last season, he has created more chances than any other player in the Champions League (44), while also making the joint-most defensive line-breaking passes (43). Only Lamine Yamal (55) has completed more dribbles than the Frenchman (54).

Either Arsenal academy graduate Serge Gnabry or promising youngster Lennart Karl will likely come in on the right flank, and the good news for the hosts is that they still have plenty of firepower in their ranks, even with Olise missing.

This will be Harry Kane‘s penultimate game before he discovers whether he has become the first Englishman to win the Ballon d'Or since Michael Owen in 2001, with the winner of football's most prestigious individual award announced next week.
And Kane, who marked his 100th Bundesliga appearance with his 102nd goal in the competition on Saturday, has an excellent record against Arsenal.
The former Tottenham hero has scored 15 goals in 22 career appearances against the Gunners, only netting more against Leicester City (20) and Everton (16).

England's captain will be going up against the Premier League‘s best defensive unit, with Arsenal remaining within three points of Manchester City domestically following Sunday's hard-earned 1-0 win at Nottingham Forest.

Noni Madueke came off the bench to settle that encounter with a deflected strike, and although there were a few nervy moments late on, Arsenal held on for their 32nd 1-0 win in the Premier League under Mikel Arteta – the joint-most of any team since he took charge in December 2019 (alongside Everton).

The Gunners are one of nine teams to have maximum points on the board in the Champions League, following last week's 3-0 victory over Lille. Bukayo Saka played a starring role in that success, coming off the bench to provide a goal and assist, and he is primed to play a key part here.

Just four of Saka's 14 Champions League goals have come away from home, though two of those were against Real Madrid and Paris Saint-Germain. Only two players have ever scored away against all three of Bayern Munich, Real Madrid and PSG in the competition – Didier Drogba and Erling Haaland.

Given Bayern's commitment to dominating possession, it remains to be seen just how aggressive Arsenal will be – they attracted criticism for their tentative approach in last season's final versus PSG, recording the lowest possession share on record by any team in a Champions League showpiece (since 2003-04, 24.7%).
However, 73% of Arsenal's high-intensity pressures in the Champions League this season have been in the opposition half (373/508), the highest percentage by any team through the first two matchdays.
The Gunners also led all teams for high turnovers (25) and shot-ending high turnovers (9) in the opening two rounds of fixtures, so they certainly have it in them play proactively.

Arsenal have also won each of their last 14 league-stage matches in UEFA's top-tier competition, with only PSG and Real Madrid (28 each) having won more Champions League games overall than the Gunners since their 2023 return (27, level with Bayern).
